lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The resume lacks a clear target-role headline or summary.
items.because: Recruiters must infer whether the target is machine learning, software, research, or LLM/agent infrastructure engineering.

items.says: The Mobility Systems bullets are not ordered by importance; the production triage result should lead and the evaluation harness should appear earlier.
items.because: The current order postpones the clearest production impact and a distinctive evaluation contribution.

items.says: The Eastern Robotics bullets should be reordered for the target role.
items.because: ML platform roles and robotics or distributed-systems roles call for different priorities.

items.says: The research-engineering and production-engineering narratives need a more coherent connecting theme.
items.because: Otherwise readers may see an unfocused transition from robotics to LLMs.

items.says: The skills section is too thin for the technical depth demonstrated elsewhere.
items.because: Recruiters searching for relevant terms may miss capabilities in ML systems, evaluation, concurrency, event-driven architecture, inference optimization, CI/CD, and statistical evaluation.

items.says: Relevant frameworks and platforms actually used should be represented in the skills section.
items.because: The resume feels technically richer than the skills list and currently undersells the candidate.

items.says: Terms such as inference, model serving, distributed systems, LLMs, deployment, monitoring, testing, and release automation are missing or underrepresented if applicable.
items.because: These capabilities are implied rather than explicit, which may weaken ATS matching.

items.says: Tense should be standardized across past experience and the current project.
items.because: Experience bullets should consistently use past tense and current-project bullets should consistently use present tense.

items.says: Technical terminology and hyphenation should be standardized.
items.because: Inconsistent styling can make the resume look assembled from different drafts.

items.says: Several bullets wrap in awkward places.
items.because: Poor wrapping of technical phrases and dependent clauses makes the document look less polished.

items.says: The resume is too dense and may be difficult to scan.
items.because: Duplicated and generic material should be removed before reducing the font size.

items.says: The portfolio link should be checked for relevant projects, readable documentation, and completed public repositories.
items.because: A code portfolio is useful only when it demonstrates the engineering decisions implied by the resume.

items.says: The date of birth should be removed.
items.because: It is unnecessary on a North American technical resume and can create age-discrimination concerns.

items.says: Nationality should be removed unless a relevant, accurate work-authorization statement is needed instead.
items.because: Nationality is normally omitted and does not establish qualification for the role.

items.says: The expected degree status should state more clearly that the degree is in progress.
items.because: Employers may distinguish a completed graduate degree from current enrollment.

items.says: The institution name, location, and degree name should be verified or placeholders replaced before applying.
items.because: Anonymized names must be replaced, while actual details must be accurate and consistently formatted.

items.says: The institution name, location, and degree name should be verified or placeholders replaced before applying.
items.because: Anonymized names must be replaced, while actual details must be accurate and consistently formatted.

items.says: “Diagnostic accuracy” is not defined.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it means exact-match, case-level resolution, classification, retrieval, or another measure.

items.says: The baseline for the 35% improvement is unclear.
items.because: The result is more credible when readers know whether it was measured against the original model, a prior adapter, or a production baseline.

items.says: “Validated tool-use trajectories” is not self-explanatory.
items.because: General recruiters may not understand that these were quality-controlled examples of tool-using model behavior.

items.says: The reviewer-disagreement metric is ambiguous.
items.because: It could mean incorrect reviewer conclusions, conflicting outputs, or a failed consistency check.

items.says: Ownership of the routing layer should be clarified.
items.because: The reader needs to know which parts were designed, implemented, evaluated, and deployed.

items.says: The bullet is overloaded with agents, scope controls, and percentages.
items.because: Its density may force readers to reread it instead of quickly seeing the architecture and outcome.

items.says: The “at equal accuracy” evaluation condition should be more prominent.
items.because: It shows that reduced tool use did not come at the cost of quality.

items.says: The candidate's role in the GRPO work is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish ownership of training design, reward design, rollout collection, or execution of an existing implementation.

items.says: The 5% latency reduction may not be meaningful enough without a baseline or operational context.
items.because: The 18% tool-call reduction is stronger unless the latency change mattered in production.

items.says: “Citation quality” is too broad.
items.because: It could refer to citation correctness, source attribution, completeness, or another property.

items.says: The extent of team adoption of the evaluation harness is unclear.
items.because: It would be stronger to show whether it became part of CI, the release process, or a standard benchmark.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking bullet duplicates the mechanism already stated in line 9 and should be removed or merged.
items.because: Repetition consumes space and makes the experience section look less substantial.

items.says: “So the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully” overstates the causal role of loss masking.
items.because: The behavior may have resulted from the data, adapter, masking strategy, or all three.

items.says: The candidate's relationship to the launch and rollout is unclear.
items.because: The reader should know whether the candidate built, deployed, owned, or evaluated the triage branch.

items.says: The business meaning of the pending-case backlog is vague.
items.because: It is unclear whether it affected maintenance cases, engineering queues, customer response time, or inspection throughput.

items.says: The meaning of the 4x GPU-memory reduction is unclear.
items.because: The figure could refer to peak allocation, total training footprint, or per-device memory.

items.says: The operational consequence of the memory reduction is missing.
items.because: The reader does not know whether it enabled larger batches, longer sequences, larger models, fewer GPUs, or lower cost.

items.says: The BF16 claim needs a defensible technical basis.
items.because: It invites questions about hardware support, numerical stability, loss scaling, and validation.

items.says: The scope of the p95 measurement is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it was end-to-end, API-layer, or specific to one operation.

items.says: “Maintained … and adds …” has inconsistent tense and subject agreement.
items.because: It shifts from past tense to a singular present-tense verb.

items.says: “Shortened release cycles to 3 days” is ambiguous.
items.because: It is unclear whether three days was the prior duration, the resulting duration, or the amount of reduction.

items.says: “Automated regression checks” is too generic.
items.because: The bullet does not specify whether the checks covered model quality, latency, software reliability, or another failure mode.

items.says: The CI regression checks are not clearly distinguished from the evaluation harness in line 12.
items.because: Each bullet should have a distinct scope for model or agent evaluation versus software or pipeline reliability.

items.says: The fleet migration needs a more measurable service impact if available.
items.because: Throughput, failure rate, dispatch impact, or operational frequency would strengthen the result beyond removing nightly backlogs.

items.says: The candidate's role in the migration is unclear.
items.because: “Migrated” may imply full ownership without distinguishing architecture, implementation, rollout, and service-owner coordination.

items.says: “Morning dispatch” lacks business context.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it was a customer-facing, logistics, warehouse, or fleet-operations process.

items.says: The AI-first engineering bullet uses vague and promotional claims instead of a concrete technical or adoption result.
items.because: “Drove adoption,” “accelerating delivery,” and “improving outcomes” provide no baseline, scale, artifact, user count, or measurable result.

items.says: The bullet does not say what the candidate personally built.
items.because: The project is labeled “Owner,” but the bullet describes broad organizational influence rather than implementation.

items.says: The adoption claim is unquantified and should be supported or removed.
items.because: Real adoption should be shown through teams, users, workflows, repositories, or deployments.

items.says: The context-management measurement setup is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not define “working context” or explain how quality was preserved while the raw conversation grew 100x.

items.says: The bullet lacks a quality or reliability outcome.
items.because: Token reduction alone may be interpreted as aggressive information loss.

items.says: The relevance of the 100-turn stress test is not explained.
items.because: The reader should know why it represents a realistic workload rather than an artificial benchmark.

items.says: The origin of the deadlocks and lost tool results is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether they were production bugs, test failures, or development risks.

items.says: The significance of 50-way fan-out is not explained.
items.because: The scale should be connected to the expected workload or stress-test design.

items.says: “Removing” deadlocks and lost results claims more certainty than the evidence shown.
items.because: The wording implies the issues no longer occur and should be supported at that level.

items.says: The candidate's contribution to the eight metrics is unclear.
items.because: “Integrated” does not show whether the candidate selected metrics, implemented logic, wrote adapters, added tests, or connected existing packages.

items.says: The evaluation dimensions are not described precisely enough.
items.because: “Citation and faithfulness metrics” does not explain which research-agent behaviors the framework evaluates.

items.says: The meaning of the Kendall correlation is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it compares evaluator scores with degradation severity, human judgments, or another reference signal.

items.says: The injected-degradation protocol is insufficiently described.
items.because: It is unclear whether degradation was controlled, random, staged, or manually designed.

items.says: The correlation should not imply broad evaluator validity.
items.because: It demonstrates sensitivity to the tested degradation, not necessarily general validity.

items.says: The industrial triage achievement duplicates line 14 and appears misplaced under the Research-Agent Evaluation Framework.
items.because: A hiring manager may interpret it as padding, a copy-paste error, or an unrelated result attributed to the project.

items.says: The placement makes chronology and ownership unclear.
items.because: Production impact belongs in the experience section unless the project made a distinct, directly related contribution.

items.says: Git is a low-signal skill if space is limited.
items.because: It is nearly universal for the target audience and should not displace more differentiating capabilities.

items.says: “Agent evaluation” is too broad.
items.because: It could mean citation evaluation, faithfulness, tool-use correctness, regression testing, benchmark construction, or human evaluation.
